## Current State
In `plugin/bin/lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.js`'s `crossReferenceKeyFiles` (line 57), sibling-title matching uses a plain lowercased substring test (`line.toLowerCase().includes(titleLower)`, line 72) with no word-boundary check — a short/generic sibling title can appear as a substring inside an unrelated longer word or phrase in another unit's Gotchas/Prerequisites text, wrongly attaching that unit's grep hits to the wrong sibling's Key Files list. Separately, `extractSection(other.body, 'Gotchas'/'Prerequisites')` (line 68) is recomputed inside the inner `for (const other of list)` loop on every outer `unit` iteration, even though each `other`'s section text doesn't depend on the outer unit — O(N^2) re-parsing for a decomposition batch of N sub-issues — and the injected `grep(ident)` subprocess call (line ~76) has no memoization across outer units sharing the same identifier, real avoidable subprocess-spawn cost that scales with batch size.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add a word-boundary check to the sibling-title substring match, reusing the existing `escapeRegExp` helper (`plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js`) to build a `\b{escaped title}\b` regex rather than writing a new escaper — the title is user-authored text and may itself contain regex metacharacters.
- [ ] Hoist the `extractSection(other.body, 'Gotchas')` / `extractSection(other.body, 'Prerequisites')` computation for each `other` outside the outer `unit` loop (compute once per `other`, into a map keyed by `other`, not once per unit×other pair).
- [ ] Memoize `grep(ident)` results (a `Map<string, string[]>`) across outer units within one `crossReferenceKeyFiles` call, so the same identifier is grepped at most once per batch regardless of how many units reference it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A test with a short generic sibling title (e.g. "Fix") that also appears as a substring of an unrelated word in another unit's Gotchas text does not wrongly cross-reference.
2. A test confirms `extractSection` is called at most once per distinct `other` unit within one batch (not once per unit×other pair) — e.g. via a call-counting wrapper or spy on a batch of 3+ units.
3. A test confirms the injected `grep` is called at most once per distinct identifier within one batch, even when multiple units' Gotchas reference the same identifier.
4. All six existing tests in `tests/bin-lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.test.js` pass unchanged.

## Technical Approach
Reuse `escapeRegExp` from `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` (already used the same way in `claim-store.js:415` to build a safe dynamic regex from untrusted text) rather than introducing a second escaping implementation. For the two performance fixes, restructure the double loop so the `other`-keyed work (section extraction) happens once per `other` before the outer `unit` loop runs, and thread a shared `Map` for grep memoization through the whole `crossReferenceKeyFiles` call.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.js` — `crossReferenceKeyFiles` (line 57), `extractSection` (line 33), the substring match (line 72), the `grep(ident)` call (line ~76)
- `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` — `escapeRegExp` (line 43), to reuse rather than reimplement
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.test.js` — 129 lines, 6 existing tests, all must stay green

## Current State
`package.json`'s `test` script (`"test": "CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 node --test $(find tests tools/upstream-drift/tests -name '*.test.js' | sort)"`) uses two POSIX-only shell constructs: a `VAR=value command` env-prefix, and `$(...)` command substitution to enumerate test files. `npm test` on Windows runs this under `cmd.exe`, which supports neither, so it fails immediately with `'CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md`'s Step 2 documents `bin/verify.js --cmd tests="npm test"` as this repo's canonical verification invocation; `verify.js` just shells out to whatever string a `--cmd` value carries (`spawnImpl(command, {shell: true})`, `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js:41`), so it inherits the failure unchanged rather than causing it. (The original request's claim that this exact failure was "already documented in this project's own memory notes" doesn't hold — no repo doc, `docs/incident-log.md`, or session memory records this specific pairing; related but distinct Windows-portability incidents exist, e.g. a path-backslash-in-string-literal bug `[IL-154]`.)

## Deliverables
- [ ] A small portable Node script (e.g. `tools/run-tests.js`) that: walks `tests/` and `tools/upstream-drift/tests/` for `*.test.js` files in JS (no shell glob), matching today's `find tests tools/upstream-drift/tests -name '*.test.js' | sort` output exactly; sets `process.env.CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = process.env.CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS || '60000'` before spawning; spawns `node --test <files>` with `stdio: 'inherit'` and exits with the child's exit code.
- [ ] `package.json`'s `test` script updated to `"node tools/run-tests.js"` (or equivalent), removing the env-prefix and `$(...)` constructs entirely — fixing the shell portability at the source, so `verification.md`'s documented `--cmd tests="npm test"` invocation needs no Windows-specific alternative and stays unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The new script's resolved file list is identical (same set, no additions or omissions) to `find tests tools/upstream-drift/tests -name '*.test.js' | sort`'s current output (549 files as of this writing) — verify by diffing the two lists.
2. `npm test`'s underlying invocation contains neither a POSIX env-prefix (`VAR=value cmd`) nor `$(...)` command substitution (verified by inspection; a live `cmd.exe` run isn't available on this build's host, so this AC is a code-shape check, not an on-host proof).
3. `CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` still resolves to `60000` during `npm test` when the caller hasn't set it (unchanged from today — `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js`'s `resolveTimeout` reads it via `process.env`).
4. `npm test` still passes in full on this (POSIX) host after the change.

## Technical Approach
Fix the shell-portability problem once at its source (`package.json`'s script) rather than teaching every consumer — `verify.js`'s documented example, any human running `npm test` directly — a Windows-specific workaround. `CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`'s default is a widen-for-tests override, not a correctness requirement: `resolveTimeout` (`git-exec.js`) already falls back to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` when the env var is unset or non-numeric, so even a script bug that failed to set it would degrade to today's production timeout rather than break test execution outright — the script should still set it, though, to keep parity with today's wider test-only timeout.

- `package.json` — the `test` script (line 7)
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js` — `resolveTimeout` (line ~50), confirms the env var has a safe fallback
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js:41` — confirms `verify.js` just shells out to the `--cmd` string unchanged, so no separate `verify.js` fix is needed once `npm test` itself is portable

- `docs/incident-log.md:421` documents a precedent directly on point: a prior change to `package.json`'s test-file enumeration silently dropped a whole new module's tests from `npm test` without any red signal — "the suite gets quieter, not redder." AC1's exact-diff check exists specifically to catch that failure mode here.
- No live Windows/`cmd.exe` host is available in this environment to run AC2 end-to-end; it is verified by removing the two named incompatible shell constructs, not by an on-host pass.

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/ports/ensure.js`'s `ensure()` reads and parses `.env.local`'s managed region twice on the path that matters most: an existing lease whose bound port is not free (the common case at every subsequent session start against an already-running dev server). It reads once unconditionally as `regionBefore` (line ~70), then `isRegionCurrent()` (line 34) re-reads and re-parses the same unmodified file itself at line 90, with no write between the two reads.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Extract a `regionIsCurrent(region, base, leaseServices, policyServices)` helper that takes an already-parsed region array (the `readManagedRegion()` return value) instead of a checkout path, containing today's `isRegionCurrent` comparison logic (PORT match + `sameServices`).
- [ ] Keep `isRegionCurrent(checkoutRoot, base, leaseServices, policyServices)` exported with its current signature and behavior, reimplemented as a thin wrapper: read `.env.local`, parse it, delegate to `regionIsCurrent`.
- [ ] In `ensure()`, replace the `isRegionCurrent(checkoutRoot, base, lease.services, policyServices)` call with `regionIsCurrent(regionBefore, base, lease.services, policyServices)`, reusing the region already read into `regionBefore`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `ensure()` reads `.env.local` at most once per invocation for the managed-region check (verify via a spy/count on `fs.readFileSync` in a test exercising the existing-lease-not-free branch).
2. Existing `tests/bin-lib/ports/ensure.test.js` assertions pass unchanged — `isRegionCurrent`'s signature and behavior (checkout-root-in, boolean-out) are untouched, only its internals delegate.

## Technical Approach
Keeping `isRegionCurrent`'s public signature intact is required, not optional: it's exported (`module.exports`) and five assertions in `tests/bin-lib/ports/ensure.test.js` (lines 121, 181, 184, 187, 188) call it directly as `isRegionCurrent(dir, base, leaseServices, policyServices)` against a checkout path. Changing that signature to take a pre-parsed region would fail AC2. The fix instead splits the comparison logic out into a new `regionIsCurrent(region, ...)` that both `isRegionCurrent` (file-reading wrapper, for the standalone tests and any other caller) and `ensure()` (already holding `regionBefore`) can call — only `ensure()`'s internal call site changes.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/ports/ensure.js` — `isRegionCurrent` (line 34), `regionBefore` read (line ~70), the call site at line 90 to redirect
- `tests/bin-lib/ports/ensure.test.js` — existing `isRegionCurrent` assertions that must keep passing unchanged; no new test required by the ACs beyond the read-count check in AC1, but the existing-lease-not-free branch (`stillFree` false, `isRegionCurrent`-equivalent true) should be the one exercised

## Gotchas
- `isRegionCurrent`'s own missing-file branch returns `false` before ever calling `readManagedRegion` — `regionIsCurrent` must treat a `null`/falsy `region` argument the same way (`if (!region) return false;`), matching `readManagedRegion`'s existing `if (!region) return false;` check inside the current function body.
- The two reads only both happen on one branch (existing lease AND port not free) — `!existingEntry` and `existingEntry && stillFree` never call `isRegionCurrent` at all today, so this is a hot-path optimization for the "server already running" case, not a fix that touches every call.

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` attributes a `skill_invoked` event to a phase by name: a `claude-tweaks:*` skill that is one of the ten `PHASES` opens that phase, a skill listed in `NESTED_PARENT` (`simplify`, `reflect`, `visual-review`, `capture`, `design-wrapper`, `challenge`, `assess-agent-autonomy`, `ledger`, `journeys`, all mapped to `'enclosing'`) attributes to the phase that is already open, and — by the file's own comment — "an un-mapped `claude-tweaks:*` skill_invoked event opens a new top-level phase named after the skill", so that "a maintainer adding a new nested-skill call site inside review/wrap-up/build must add its name here, or every run will grow a spurious top-level phase." Nothing enforces that sentence. The only test touching the roster is `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js`'s `NESTED_PARENT.journeys === 'enclosing'` pin. The sibling roster for ceremony skip tags is pinned by `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`, which walks `plugin/skills/**` and asserts every fast-lane skip mention in the corpus carries a rostered tag — the shape this record asks for.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js`: walks the phase-skill directories (`build`, `test`, `review`, `design-wrapper`, `wrap-up`, `flow`, and their `_shared/` contracts) and collects every `/claude-tweaks:{name}` invocation that appears *outside* a `## Next Actions` block (Next Actions lines are human launchers, not nested Skill-tool calls) and outside fenced code blocks that render commands for a human; each collected `{name}` must be a `PHASES` member, a `NESTED_PARENT` key, or on a small, commented allowlist of skills that are named descriptively but never invoked from a phase (e.g. `specify` cited as the upstream, `sweep` as the orchestrator). The assertion message names the file, line, and skill so the fix is one roster entry.
- [ ] A second assertion in the same file: every `NESTED_PARENT` key is invoked somewhere in that scan, so a stale entry (a nested skill that no phase skill calls any more) is reported rather than carried forever.
- [ ] A comment on `NESTED_PARENT` pointing at the test by name, replacing the "must add its name here" sentence's implicit trust with the explicit pin.
- [ ] The existing `derive.test.js` pin stays; `npm test` picks the new file up via the recursive glob (no registration).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Deleting any current `NESTED_PARENT` key makes the new test fail naming a real call site in the corpus (each of the nine keys is exercised).
2. Adding a `/claude-tweaks:{new}` invocation inside a phase skill's step body without a roster entry makes the test fail with file, line, and skill name; adding the entry makes it pass.
3. A `/claude-tweaks:{name}` under a `## Next Actions` heading or inside a human-facing fenced command block does not trip the test.
4. The test passes on the current corpus; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Scan the corpus the way the ceremony roster test does (walk `plugin/skills`, read each file, regex per line) rather than parsing `docs/skill-graph.md`: the graph rows are prose and describe every relationship kind, while the timing roster cares only about what a phase skill *invokes* mid-phase, which is exactly what the phase directories' step bodies say. The `## Next Actions` exclusion is the load-bearing heuristic — every phase skill ends with a launcher block naming skills it does not invoke — so the scanner tracks the current `##` heading while walking lines. The stale-key assertion is the half the ceremony test lacks and the cheap half to add, since the scan already produces the invoked set.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` — `PHASES`, `NESTED_PARENT`, `isTopLevel`, the roster comment.
- `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` — the corpus-walk template (`walk`, per-line regex, heading tracking).
- `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js` — existing pin (unchanged).
- `plugin/skills/{build,test,review,design-wrapper,wrap-up,flow}/**` and `plugin/skills/_shared/**` — the scanned corpus.

## Gotchas
- `skill_invoked` events exist only for model-initiated Skill calls, so a skill a phase names only in prose ("see `/claude-tweaks:specify`") never produces an event; that is why the scan needs an allowlist for descriptive mentions and why the allowlist must stay short and commented — a growing allowlist is the roster problem moved.
- `PHASES` names (`test`, `review`, `polish`, `wrap-up`) are themselves skills invoked by `/flow`; they are top-level by design and must be excluded from the nested check, not added to `NESTED_PARENT`.
- `design-wrapper` is invoked as the `polish` phase by `/flow` (top-level there) and as a nested call from `/review` (Step 3.8 craft critics); `NESTED_PARENT` maps it to `'enclosing'` and `derive.js` resolves the polish phase separately — the test asserts roster membership only, never phase semantics.
- Keep the scan to the phase directories; `backlog`, `tidy`, and `sweep` invoke many skills but never run inside a timed pipeline phase.

Surface: infra

## Current State
`/claude-tweaks:review` dispatches up to a dozen agents per run — reproduction-pair lens agents (`step3-lens-dispatch.md`, 3a–3f), cross-lens debate judges and per-candidate refutation agents (`step3-debate-and-refutation.md`, Step 3.5), and the gap-sweep critic (Step 3.6) — each with "fresh read access to the actual current file content" and no instruction about where to put anything they write. The main thread already has a per-review scratch directory: `build-review-context.js mint` produces `{ctx-dir}` (`{run}/review-ctx` under a pipeline run, a unique system-temp directory otherwise), and every file the *skill* writes (`lens-*.json`, `findings-by-lens.json`) lives there. The dispatch prompts hand agents the bundle path inside it but never say "write your probe scripts here"; an agent that wants to execute a snippet drops `zz-*.mts` or `__bench_*.mjs` in the worktree root or beside the module under review. The only untracked-file check in the skill is the post-dispatch diff audit in `step3-routing.md`, which runs `git status --porcelain` after *fix* agents return, not after the lens/refutation/gap-sweep fan-out. Observed cost on a 12-agent `xhigh` review: a false architecture finding ("throwaway debug script committed in the module directory" — an untracked sibling-agent leftover), `tsc` errors for a later implementer from a reviewer's stray file, and four manual `rm` sweeps. Nothing was committed only because every commit used explicit paths. (The record names `curation-engine.md` as the sweep site; that file belongs to `/wrap-up`'s curation registry, and the review-side collection points are the ones above.)

## Deliverables
- [ ] One "Scratch rule" paragraph in `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s input-discipline section, stated once and cited by every dispatch template that hands an agent write access: any file an agent creates to verify its work (probe script, benchmark, fixture) goes under the scratch directory the prompt names, never under the repository tree; the agent deletes what it created before its status word; a dispatch prompt that gives an agent write access must name a scratch path.
- [ ] The three review dispatch templates (`step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s per-lens Calibration/Output template's *outer* prompt, not the byte-identical Calibration block; `step3-debate-and-refutation.md`'s refutation and gap-sweep templates) gain a `SCRATCH: {ctx-dir}/agent-scratch/{agent-id}` line, minted per dispatch under the existing `{ctx-dir}`, and cite the contract's Scratch rule. Debate judges write nothing and get no line.
- [ ] A post-fan-out untracked-file sweep in `step3-lens-dispatch.md`, run once after every reproduction pair (and, at `high`+, after Step 3.5/3.6) has returned and before Step 3 Routing: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` diffed against the same listing captured before the first dispatch; any new untracked path outside `{ctx-dir}` is reported by name, logged as `STAGED {time} — Review fan-out left {n} untracked file(s): {paths}. Not deleted. Reversibility: n/a.`, and excluded from the findings a reviewer sees (a finding whose only evidence is one of those paths is downgraded to `unconfirmed` with that reason). Deletion is not automatic here: the sweep names files, the controller decides — the `sweep-shadow` analogy the record draws is a move, not a delete, and a reviewer's leftover could be a sibling implementer's in-flight file.
- [ ] `step3-routing.md`'s existing post-dispatch diff audit gains one sentence pointing at the fan-out sweep as its sibling, so the two untracked checks are visibly one rule applied twice.
- [ ] Tests: `tests/multi-agent-coordination.test.js` (which pins `step3-lens-dispatch.md`) keeps its byte-identical-block assertion unchanged and gains pins for the `SCRATCH:` line in each of the three templates and the fan-out sweep's `STAGED` line shape; `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` pins the contract's Scratch rule heading.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every review dispatch template that grants write access names a scratch path under `{ctx-dir}` and cites the contract rule; the Calibration/Output block stays byte-identical (its existing pin proves it).
2. After the fan-out, a new untracked file outside `{ctx-dir}` is named in the review output and `decisions.md`, and cannot become the sole evidence of a `confirmed` finding.
3. No agent-created file is deleted by the skill; the sweep reports, the controller decides.
4. `npm test` is green, including the unchanged byte-identical-template pin.

## Technical Approach
Use the scratch directory that already exists rather than inventing a second one: `{ctx-dir}` is per-review, per-run unique, avoids the `tmp/` path segment the permissions deny-glob matches (refs #1213), and is already the home of the skill's own scratch files, so an agent-scratch subdirectory under it needs no new minting or cleanup path (`/wrap-up` archives the run dir with it). Put the rule in the contract, not in each template: the record's own repro spans three templates, and the next fan-out site (`/design-wrapper`'s craft critics, `/docs-health`'s per-target dispatch) would otherwise re-derive it. Report-don't-delete for the sweep because a reviewer cannot distinguish its own agents' leftovers from a concurrent implementer's untracked work in the same worktree.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — input discipline section (new Scratch rule).
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — reproduction dispatch prompt, the pre-dispatch listing capture, the post-fan-out sweep.
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-debate-and-refutation.md` — refutation template (Step 3.5 step 4) and gap-sweep template (Step 3.6).
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — post-dispatch diff audit paragraph.
- `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js` — `mint` (read-only reference for `{ctx-dir}`'s shape; no change unless a subdirectory helper is wanted).
- `tests/multi-agent-coordination.test.js`, `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — prose pins.

## Gotchas
- The per-lens Calibration + Output block must stay byte-identical across all tiers (the cross-lens reproduction logic depends on it); the `SCRATCH:` line goes in the outer prompt beside the scope and `Path:Line` instructions, exactly where `step3-lens-dispatch.md` already places per-dispatch text.
- `--untracked-files=all` matters: the default `git status --porcelain` collapses a new directory to one line and would hide a probe script inside a freshly created folder.
- `{ctx-dir}` under a pipeline run is committed with the run dir's archive by `/wrap-up`; keep agent scratch small or add `agent-scratch/` to the run dir's ignore rules — `_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s "Pipeline run directory" section owns the layout and gitignore treatment; check it before choosing.
- Agents under `EnterWorktree`-based isolation cannot chain commands (contract's Shell constraint); the cleanup instruction must be one plain `rm` per file, not a `find … -delete`.

## Original request
**Summary:** Lens, refutation and gap-sweep agents dispatched during `/review` write probe scripts wherever is convenient inside the worktree, including inside the module under review, with no mandated scratch location and no controller sweep to catch what's left behind.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/review` lens, refutation and gap-sweep dispatch templates; `curation-engine.md` post-fan-out sweep

**Use case:** A multi-agent review run (lens agents 3b-3f, refutation agents, the gap-sweep agent) needs to run probe scripts to verify findings, without leaving stray untracked files that pollute the worktree for later steps or other agents.

**Repro steps:**
1. Run a review with several dispatched lens/refutation/gap-sweep agents (observed on a 12-agent `xhigh` review).
2. Let one or more agents write ad hoc probe scripts (e.g. `zz-*.mts`, `__bench_*.mjs`) directly in the worktree root or inside the module under review.
3. Let the fan-out complete without an explicit cleanup step.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: probe scripts either never touch the tracked worktree, or are swept up automatically before the fan-out's results are trusted.
Actual: in one run this produced a false architecture finding ("throwaway debug script committed in the module directory" — it was actually untracked, left by a sibling agent), tsc errors for a later implementer caused by a reviewer's stray file, and four manual `rm` sweeps by the controller. Nothing was actually committed only because every commit used explicit paths rather than `git add -A`.

**Suggestion:** (1) the per-lens / refutation / gap-sweep dispatch templates name a scratch location outside the repo (`os.tmpdir()`-based, or the run dir's own scratch subdirectory) and require cleanup before the status word; (2) the controller's post-fan-out sweep runs `git status --porcelain` and reports or deletes untracked files that appeared during the fan-out, the same way `sweep-shadow` handles stray staged files.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

## Current State

`skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Overview states: "When invoked by `/claude-tweaks:flow`, review runs in **full** mode by default (code + visual)." But the Input resolution section's actual mode-selection rules (1-8) are purely token-based — the literal word `full` appearing in `$ARGUMENTS` is the only thing that selects full mode. There is no rule that checks `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` (or any other flow-context signal) and defaults to full mode when no explicit mode token is present. A flow executor who invokes `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` without typing `full` explicitly silently gets **code** mode instead — no warning, no divergence from the documented default surfaced anywhere. This run (#1143's own flow continuation) hit exactly this gap: `/claude-tweaks:review #1143` was invoked without the `full` token, resolving to code mode per the skill's own Input resolution rule 1. `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` line 30 states verbatim: "Begin stop is opt-in under `auto`. `/flow` defaults to `auto`, and in `auto` the Manifesto renders as a **read-only FYI** ... so the everyday auto pipeline has effectively **one** user-facing stop ... The 'at most two stops' promise is a ceiling, not a floor." ## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
claude-tweaks pipelines have at most two stops in `auto` mode: a **Pipeline Config Manifesto** at the start (one structured numbered-options block collecting all policy levers in a single message) and a **Wrap-Up Review Console** at the end (one batch table consolidating everything auto-decided or staged). Everything in between is policy-driven automation logged to the auto-decision log.
```

**Proposed:**
```
claude-tweaks pipelines have at most two stops in `auto` mode: a **Pipeline Config Manifesto** at the start (one structured numbered-options block collecting all policy levers in a single message) and a **Wrap-Up Review Console** at the end (one batch table consolidating everything auto-decided or staged). The two-stop ceiling isn't a floor: in default `auto`, the Manifesto renders as a **read-only FYI** (displays levers, doesn't gate), so the everyday run has effectively **one** user-facing stop — the end Review Console. Pass `confirm` (or `hybrid`) to turn the Manifesto into a real approval gate. Everything in between is policy-driven automation logged to the auto-decision log.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

CLAUDE.md's Auto-Mode Contract paragraph presents "at most two stops" as if both stops normally occur in `auto` mode, but the canonical `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` (the file this paragraph cites as single source of truth) now explicitly clarifies that the ceiling is not a floor: in default `auto`, the Manifesto renders as a read-only FYI and never gates, so the everyday auto run has effectively only one user-facing stop (the end Review Console) — the Manifesto only becomes a real stop under `confirm`/`hybrid`.

## Current State

#647's expand phase shipped per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` (`permittedGrants`), fixing a bug where the flat top-level `reason` string could pair a granted `bornReady` with the other grant's denial text. The flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys were kept as a transitional twin, with the module header (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, lines ~10-15) recording a removal condition: delete the flat keys at the first release on or after 2026-11-16 (ship date + 3 months, per `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape).

Two skill-text consumers carry a matching read-side fallback, tagged with the same removal condition: `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (line ~144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (line ~223), both doing `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }`.

Confirmed at shaping time (2026-08-17): the module header text, both fallback call sites, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line (`↳ trust: {provenance} / {band} — {verdict}{, {coverage}% coverage}`) all reproduce exactly as described — the trust-table snippet's `bornReady`/`reason` output fields (written to `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) are genuinely dead: nothing downstream reads or renders them.

The removal date (2026-11-16) has **not** yet passed as of this record's shaping (2026-08-17) — it is roughly three months out. This record documents and prepares the contract phase; it does not authorize building the removal before that date.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Verify, at build time, that the current date is on or after 2026-11-16 (the first release on/after that date) before making any of the changes below. If built before that date, stop without editing anything and report the record as not yet actionable — see Acceptance Criteria #1, a hard gate.
- [ ] Re-run `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` to confirm every consumer still reads only `grants.*` shapes (no new flat-key consumer introduced since shaping).
- [ ] Remove the flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys from `permittedGrants`'s return value in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, and delete the module-header comment block documenting the now-resolved removal condition.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (the `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` pattern and its explanatory comment), reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (same pattern, same treatment).
- [ ] Drop the dead `bornReady`/`reason` output fields from `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet (the `node -e` block that writes `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) — confirmed nothing downstream (`skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line) reads them.
- [ ] Decide, and record the decision inline as a code/skill-text comment, how to handle the two disclosed conflation residues before deleting the flat keys:
  1. Withheld grants share one reason string today — `grants.bornAuthorized.reason` can carry born-ready's rationale on the human-filed path. Decide whether this stays as-is (the per-grant shape already fixes the *granted*-path pairing bug; the withheld-grant sharing is a separate, lower-severity residue) or gets its own follow-up record.
  2. The granted path's flat `reason` today carries positive rationale text ("class is clean, ceiling is unattended, grant origination opted in") that no per-grant key reproduces. Decide whether to populate that positive rationale into the granted per-grant `reason` field, or record explicitly (in a code comment) that it is intentionally dropped as noise once the grant itself is visible via `granted: true`.
- [ ] Update or remove the flat-key compat tests in the `bin-lib/issues` test suite to match the per-grant-only shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hard precondition, checked first:** the build only proceeds once the current date is on or after 2026-11-16. A build attempted before that date stops without modifying any file and reports the record as not yet actionable — this is not a normal "build failed" outcome, it is the record's own documented gate.
2. `permittedGrants` (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`) returns only the per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` shape — no flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys at the top level.
3. No consumer (code or skill text, across `skills/` and `bin/`) reads the flat keys or carries a fallback for them — confirmed via `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` read against every hit.
4. `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet no longer computes or emits `bornReady`/`reason` fields.
5. The two conflation-residue decisions are recorded (as a comment near the code they affect, or in this record's own close-out note) — not silently dropped.
6. `npm test` passes with the flat-key compat tests updated or removed.

## Technical Approach

Start with the grep re-verification (Deliverables item 2) — the module header itself calls this out as the first step, since a consumer could have appeared between #647 shipping and this record's execution.

`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`: delete the flat keys from `permittedGrants`'s two return objects (denied-path and granted-path, around current lines 128-155) and the header comment block (lines 10-15) documenting the removal condition — the condition is satisfied, not evergreen.

`skills/capture/SKILL.md` (~line 144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (~line 223): drop the `|| { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` fallback half of each destructure, reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly; delete the accompanying "older installed build" comment.

`skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table `node -e` block (~lines 219-234): remove `bornReady`/`reason` from the `out[issue.number]` object literal.

Fold the two conflation-residue decisions into the same edit pass — they're small text/comment changes, not separate work.

Grep the `bin-lib/issues` test directory for `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized` flat-key assertions on `permittedGrants`'s return value and update/remove them alongside the source change, in the same commit.

## Gotchas

- **Date gate is load-bearing, not advisory.** This record was shaped on 2026-08-17, roughly three months before the 2026-11-16 backstop. Confirmed by reading `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`'s own module header, which states the removal condition explicitly and cites `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape as precedent for this pattern (see also #628/#629, which apply the same shape to `policy.yml` key retirements). Marking this record `ready` reflects that it is *shaped* and *queued*, not that it is *buildable today* — `/specify` has no mechanism to hold a record out of `ready` pending a future calendar date (only `parked` + `Trigger:` does that, and only `/tidy`/`/wrap-up`/`/reflect`/`/review`'s Defer paths can add it), so this Gotcha and Acceptance Criterion 1 are the only gate. Whoever dispatches this record (`/flow`, `/build`, or a human) must re-check the date before touching code.
- **Information loss is real if the conflation residues are skipped.** Deleting the flat keys without deciding the two residues (the Deliverables item above them) silently drops the granted-path's positive rationale text — no per-grant key reproduces it today. This isn't a formatting nit; a human reading a future trust/grant explanation loses the "why" for a clean grant unless this is deliberately decided and recorded.
- **Verified against live code at shaping time**, not taken on faith from the issue text: read `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` lines 1-40 (module header and `permittedGrants`), `skills/capture/SKILL.md` line ~144, `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` lines ~203-235, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md` lines ~75-100 (the rendered trust-consequence template, confirming it never references `bornReady`/`reason`). All three deliverables reproduce exactly as the original request states — no false premise to correct here.
